title: Approval status mirror: a write that does not land, a run that ends between two steps, and a decision whose run cannot resume must not leave a document closed on an unfinished approval (ADR-0162 item 8)
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ③ maintainer-directed · Source: ADR-0162 Execution item 8 (accepted by merge 972114df)

## 维护者速读

- 做什么：补上发起审批时检查不出来的三种情况：应用自己的规则拒绝了审批状态的写入、流程在两步审批之间出错或被取消、审批决定已记录但流程无法继续。三种情况下都不能让单据停在「已批准并锁住」而后面的审批其实没走完。
- 用户会看到什么：出现这三种情况时，单据不会假装已批准；状态写入被拒不再悄悄吞掉，管理员能看到哪张单据卡住了、为什么。
- 不做会怎样：这三种情况虽少见，但一旦发生，单据会带着一个没走完的审批结果被锁死，用户改不了，只能靠管理员手工处理。
- 顺序：「声明与执行」那张卡要等这张卡；这张卡开工前有几处做法需要先定。

## What happens

ADR-0162 D5 refuses, when an approval opens, every configuration it can read ahead that would leave a document on an earlier step's outcome (item 7). Three things cannot be read ahead, and each can leave a record closed on a value its own approval wrote and did not finish:

- **A write of the mirror that does not land.** A validation rule or a hook of the app refuses it, or a `visibleWhen` on an option the mirror puts back does. On `main` a failed write of the mirror is logged and swallowed, on every transition (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts#mirrorStatusField`).
- **A run that ends between two steps.** A node fails, or the run is cancelled. The next step itself can fail to open, by the policy its own configuration declares for an empty slate (`packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts#onEmptyApprovers`), or because another request is pending on the record (`approval-service.ts#openNodeRequest`). A node can also fail on the closed-state lock through a write the check cannot read: a hook that writes back to the record, or a delete on another object whose cascade reaches it. No request is open then, so none of the three writers that abandon a request acts, and the sweep of dead runs reads pending requests only (`approval-service.ts#releaseDeadRunRequests`).
- **A decision that is recorded while its run cannot be resumed**, so that the next step is never asked. `main` has a reader of such requests that reports them and changes nothing (`approval-service.ts#inspectStrandedRequests`).

On `main` the same events leave the same status on the record. What the key adds is that the status may now be a closed one.

The recommendations the maintainer adopted on 2026-11-26, 「全部按推荐」 (ruling record 7200732942 on #36253, text on 7202242844), give the mirror's failed write a child card. The seat's rulings on the eighth and ninth contract reviews of ADR-0162 added the other two to it. ADR-0162 fixes what the card delivers and leaves it the means.

## Expected

**What must hold (fixed by ADR-0162 D5).** On a field the object closes on, none of the three leaves a record closed on a value its own approval wrote and did not finish. A refused write of the mirror is no longer swallowed. An end after the last step is another case: there the approval is finished and its decision stands.

**What this card settles (left to it by the record).**
- How a refused write of the mirror is shown, and to whom.
- How the plugin learns that an approval's run has ended, or will not go on.
- How it tells a stop between two steps from one after the last step.
- Where the decision of the earlier step stands afterwards.
- What the platform then does with the record.

The record names two starting points. For the refused write, the first candidate is to set the object's rules aside for that one write (ADR-0162 "Alternatives considered"). For a run that will not go on, the reader of stranded requests on `main` is the starting point. Either may change what an app's own rules can refuse, so the choices are written up for the seat before the build starts, and the seat decides which of them go to the maintainer.

## Carried from the contract reviews of ADR-0162

- **A failed mirror write on any transition (N24).** The swallow is the same on every transition, not only on an abandoned request. The card covers each transition that writes the mirror.
- **A failure the flow routes (N46).** A flow can route a node's failure and go on, and a run can then complete without the next step having been asked. The card says on which side of its bound that falls: the author's own routing, as a branch that skips a step is, or an end between two steps. A test pins it.

## Done when

- [ ] The five questions above are answered in a design note on this card, and the seat has ruled it or taken the open ones to the maintainer.
- [ ] A refused write of the mirror on a closing field: not swallowed, shown as the note says, and the record is not left closed on the value its approval wrote. Tested for a validation rule, a hook, and a `visibleWhen` on a value the mirror puts back.
- [ ] A run that ends between two steps: tested for a node that fails, a cancelled run, a next step that fails to open on an empty slate and on a request already pending on the record, and a node that fails on the closed-state lock through a hook's write-back and through another object's cascade.
- [ ] A decision whose run cannot be resumed: the record is not left closed on that decision, and the case is visible to an administrator.
- [ ] An end after the last step leaves the decision standing, with a test.
- [ ] The routed-failure case (N46) is on the side the note names, with a test.
- [ ] Each test records the value the field keeps.
- [ ] The approvals guide (item 7, slice D) says what an author and an administrator see in each case.
- [ ] The release rule holds: the key (item 1) is not published before this card is built.

Category ③: maintainer-directed. A build card of ADR-0162, child of #36253.
Grade: area:data · Feature · n/a (not a defect on `main`; it becomes one the day the key ships without it) · reach: an approval of several steps on an object that closes on its outcome, when one of the three events happens · evidence: read (ADR-0162 D5 "What the conditions do not reach" and its Readings)
Suggested-grade: p2 · it gates the release of #36253's key, so it takes the grade of the card it blocks
Size: L (it needs design rulings before it is built). The design note is S; the build is M once the note is ruled.
Business reason: carried from #36253 and the ruling 「平台拒绝这种配置」 (7205949718): a document must not pretend to be approved. These are the cases the opening check cannot see.
Reader: seat 2 (repo:objectstack#2). First a design note by a card thread at the ADR tier, then the build at effort high.
Release-order: the root run of item 7 (slice A), which is how the plugin places a request in its approval. Like item 7's slices B and C it needs item 1's key on the same trunk branch.
Clause-②: not judged before the design note. No if the means stay inside the plugin; yes if the plugin gains a published member or a platform object gains a field.
Metadata-protocol: none expected. If the note chooses to set an object's rules aside for the mirror's write, the seat judges whether that is `semantic` for the rules concerned.
Dedupe: searched `mirrorStatusField` (open issues): 0 hits. Searched `closedStates` (all issues): 1 hit, #36253 itself.
Related: #36253, PR #37606 (ADR-0162), the card for item 7.

Dispatch note: the card thread also reads the seat's private memo for this card before it starts.
